headline: Treble raises $18 million for its voice simulation platform, bringing total funding to over $40M
summary: The Iceland-based startup's latest funding round, an extension of its Series A, brings its total raised to over $40 million. Treble's platform is used by customers like Amazon and Logitech.
details: Treble, an Iceland-based startup, has secured an additional $18 million in an extension of its Series A funding round. This latest investment brings the company's total capital raised to over $40 million, with Paladin Capital Group leading the new round.

Founded in 2020 by acoustic engineers Finnur Pind and Jesper Pedersen, Treble specializes in a voice simulation platform. This platform caters to AI model makers, robotics companies, and consumer hardware manufacturers.

The company offers synthetic data generation for speech enhancement, noise suppression, and model training for voice AI companies. It also evaluates voice AI models under various conditions, providing crucial feedback to labs.

Treble has partnered with Hugging Face to launch a benchmark for speech recognition models, emphasizing realistic conditions. Its technology aims to provide an alternative to traditional sound recordings by using accurate physics simulation for data creation.

Beyond software, Treble supports hardware design and testing, assisting headphone and speaker companies with virtual prototyping. This helps them understand product acoustics and how smart speakers interpret commands based on positioning.

The startup is also expanding into simulation testing for smart glasses and other AI devices, with a focus on wearables that could enhance hearing. This includes features like selective hearing in noisy environments.

Looking ahead, Treble plans to increase its focus on physical AI sectors such as robotics, automotive, and drones. Their platform aims to enable sound-based functions for these industries through advanced testing and simulation.

headline_marked: [[DeepSeek-v4.1 Flash achieves 4x KV Cache compression]], supports 1M token contexts
headline: DeepSeek-v4.1 Flash achieves 4x KV Cache compression, supports 1M token contexts
summary: DeepSeek-v4.1 Flash pushes KV Cache compression to the extreme, reducing storage by 4x-8x and enabling 1 million token contexts for long-horizon AI agents.
details: DeepSeek-v4.1 Flash significantly optimizes KV Cache compression, achieving a 4x reduction in runtime storage and 8x for persistent storage compared to its predecessor. This enables support for contexts up to 1 million tokens.
The model was developed to address the growing storage and computation pressure from long-horizon agent workflows, where context length and prefill computations become bottlenecks for scaling.

DeepSeek-v4.1 Flash features a 552B parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts architecture. It uses a Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) design, projecting the Encoder's final hidden states to obtain the Decoder's Global KVCache.

This architecture activates 8B parameters per token during prefill and 16B during decoding, making it highly cost-effective for input-dominated agent scenarios. The overall performance also surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
The compression techniques are a result of joint optimization across model architecture, cache precision, and deployment strategy, pushing the limits of KVCache efficiency.
